title: Inline QtWebview-based captive portal view, so you don't need to open the default browser for this
line: Logging in to a hotel or café Wi-Fi now opens a small built-in login window instead of your web browser, and it closes by itself once you're connected.
explanation: When NetworkManager detects a captive portal, the notification's Log in button, the applet's "You need to log in" banner and the tray menu's "Open Network Login Page…" all opened the connectivity check URL in the default browser. Hardened browsers, HTTPS-only modes and VPN setups often fail on the plain-HTTP portal page, the browser keeps the portal's cookies, and the browser window stays open after logging in. plasma-nm now ships a small helper (libexec plasma-nm-captive-portal, built only when Qt WebEngine is available) with an off-the-record QtWebEngine window; all three Log in actions open it through NetworkStatus::openNetworkLoginPage(), pop-ups from the portal get their own window, and the helper closes when NetworkManager reports full connectivity. Without the helper installed the actions open the browser as before.

commits.message:
captive portal: open the login page in a built-in window

The Log in actions for captive portals opened the default browser, which
may not cope with the portal page. They now open a small off-the-record
QtWebEngine window that closes once the network is fully connected.

BUG: 467991

media.caption: Master: clicking Log in on the "You need to log into this network" notification opens the default browser (here Chrome) on the hotel portal.
With the change: the same click opens a built-in "Network Login" window with the portal page.
Master: after accepting the portal the browser window just stays open on the portal's "You are connected" page.
With the change: Log in, type the room number, Accept and connect; the window closes by itself as soon as the network is fully connected.
A link the portal opens in a new window (its terms of use) gets its own window, so the login page stays where it was.
